newsitem.title: EGYPT: Use of force in Iraq aggravates situation - Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Use of force in Iraq aggravates situation - Egypt.

text.p: Egypt said on Tuesday the use of force in Iraq would aggravate the situation in the whole region, an opinion shared by the Cairo-based Arab League.
"We are all concerned about the situation in Iraq," Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told an investment conference.

"The use of force, for example what took place in north Iraq, in southern Iraq for that matter, will further aggravate the situation," Moussa said. He did distinguish between Iraqi and U.S. military actions.
The United States on Tuesday launched cruise missile strikes on air defence targets in southern Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks on Kurds in the north last weekend.
"The developments in Iraq do not augur well, neither for the people of Iraq or for the stability of the region," Moussa said.
Moussa repeated Egypt's position of support for Iraq's unity and opposition to any attempt to divide the country.
"Nothing should derogate from the fact that we, all of us, respect the territorial integrity, the political independence and sovereignty of Iraq," he added.
The Cairo-based Arab League said "the use of military force will lead only to more aggravation in the situation and expose the region to factors of tension and instability."
"The Arab League Secretary General, Esmat Abdel-Meguid, strongly denounced the (U.S.) attack, which is not based upon any international legitimacy," the league said in a statement.
"It is thus considered an infringement of an Arab country's sovereignty... and an interference in its internal affairs."
Earlier on Tuesday, a spokesman of the Egyptian foreign ministry stopped short of denouncing the U.S. missile attack.

"Egypt underlines the importance of principles and goals of the U.N. charter, which guarantee Iraq's sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-interference in its internal affairs," the spokesman said.
Egypt's most influential Islamic group, the outlawed Moslem Brotherhood, strongly condemned the U.S. attack and called for resisting it with all means.
"The American aggression against Iraq is flagrant, abhorrent and contradictory to all international laws and norms.
"We call on all parties...peoples and states, to condemn this new aggression against an Arab, Moslem and peaceful people, and resist it with all means," the group said in a statement.
